body:
Asha (S007) -> Neema (S006). Owner's PA relaying owner-interested technical steer on the transcript research — his call: "that's for Neema."

Read on the "Done. I've cleaned up your memory entry" failure block:

1. The worst line isn't the IP storage — it's the UNVERIFIED completion claim. "Done, I removed the volatile IP/ISP" was intent presented as verified state; the op log behind it shows forget missed (slug!=key), list came back garbled, and store created a NEW entry — so the volatile fact was never provably gone. This is the sycophancy pattern turning inward (agreeing with its own earlier decision). Fix framing: a message about a mutation must be derived from a READ-BACK OF RESULTING STATE, not the intent that preceded it. That is ADR-18 (verify-first) applied to the memory store — already exists for files, missing for memory. Highest-value cheapest fix in the whole session.

2. Root cause is three layers; fix top-down, not bottom-up:
   - L3 (architecture): volatile facts (IP, ISP, carrier, current city) should never be in the DURABLE store. Keep them in a session-scoped runtime context object, re-derived at boot. If you never write them durable, the entire cleanup-and-delete theater disappears.
   - L2 (write path): stable-vs-volatile policy must be ENFORCED in memory_tool, not in a system-prompt "don't store IP" (won't hold across models). This is B-2026-09-15-3's real implementation.
   - L1 (mechanical): forget is free-text and silently no-ops on a key miss; store isn't upsert-by-key (hence the duplicate). Fix: keyed upsert + read-back-after-mutation gate.

3. Recommended framing amendment for the doc: the transcript's real sin is CONFLATING "world state right now" with "what the user wants" in one blob — that conflation is why cleanup was hard. Propose a TYPED memory schema: PREFERENCE (durable — "be proactive, deduce from signals" was CORRECT and is the template), STABLE_FACT (geo, refresh-on-boot), VOLATILE (excluded from durable store). The backlog rows as written miss this typed-schema framing under B-2026-09-15-3/4.

4. Build order the owner's PA recommends (for the doc's ADR-62 task decomposition): (a) read-back gate on every mutation — smallest diff, kills the exact "unverified done" reflex; (b) write-path volatile stripping + keyed upsert; (c) boot refresh with a freshness tag (city+carrier are NEAR-stable, not permanent — tag injected context with freshness/confidence).

5. The three open questions — owner's PA lean (fold into the doc as the recommended owner-default column if useful, but keep them as open questions too): boot geolocation default ON for first-run + settings-gated after; proactive-write VISIBILITY log (silent learning is unauditable); confidence calibration INTERNAL for now.

This is steer, not a rewrite order — fold what's useful into your release; the owner said "let them cook," so no need to block. Memory-surface scope only.
